title: Vilnius Airport to Your Hotel: Your First Day
summary: Your plane lands in Vilnius, the capital of Lithuania. You are tired, but you are happy too.

cover.alt: A traveler with a sage jacket, orange backpack and amber suitcase smiles at a hotel receptionist offering a key card beside a sunlit cobbled street.

blocks.title: Introduction
paragraphs: Your plane lands in Vilnius, the capital of Lithuania. You are tired, but you are happy too. You have five questions: how to pay, how to get to the city, what to see, how to check in and what to eat. In this simulation, you take each step in time order. You learn real prices and real times. You also practise simple English for each step.

blocks.title: Warm-up

items.prompt: When you land in a new country, what do you do first?
Do you like the train, the bus or a taxi from an airport? Why?
What food do you want to try in a new country?

blocks.title: Part 1: You Land at Vilnius Airport
paragraphs: You land at Vilnius International Airport. This airport is the main airport for Vilnius. Many airlines fly here. You walk with the other people to passport control. You wait in a line. An officer looks at your passport. Then you take your bag.

Next, you think about money. Prices in Vilnius are in euros (€). For example, a bus ticket from the airport to the city centre costs €1. You buy this bus ticket from the driver. So it is good to have your payment ready before you get on the bus.
Your phone is important too. You need maps and the Bolt app. So you look for a SIM card. You do not know the price yet. Ask at the shop before you buy.

blocks.title: Check: Part 1: You Land at Vilnius Airport

items.prompt: Why is it a good idea to have your payment ready before you leave the airport?
items.answer: Prices in Vilnius are in euros. You buy the €1 bus ticket from the driver, so you must pay right away when you get on the bus.

blocks.title: Part 2: You Choose a Ride to the City
paragraphs: You have three good ways to get to the city. Each way has a different time and price.

The first way is the train. The train goes from the airport to the central railway station. The trip is 4.3 km long. It takes about 7 or 8 minutes. A ticket costs €0.45, and you can buy it online. This train is fast and cheap. But it runs only 16 times a day. So check the next train time first.

The second way is the bus. The bus takes about 15 minutes to the city centre. Several buses go to the city centre and the Old Town. You can buy a €1 ticket from the driver. City tickets cost €1 for 30 minutes or €1.25 for 60 minutes.

The third way is a taxi or a ride app. A taxi from the airport to Cathedral Square in the Old Town costs about €10. It takes about 15 minutes. You find taxis at the arrivals area. Bolt is a big ride company in Vilnius. Bolt and Uber work 24 hours a day, every day. Open the app and check the price before you say yes.

blocks.title: Check: Part 2: You Choose a Ride to the City

items.prompt: You land very late at night. The next train is not soon. What can you do, and why?
items.answer: I can take a taxi or use Bolt or Uber. They work 24 hours a day. A taxi to Cathedral Square costs about €10 and takes about 15 minutes.

blocks.title: Useful phrases

rows.term: How can I get to the Old Town?
rows.meaning: Use this to ask about the way to a place.
rows.example: Excuse me, how can I get to the Old Town?

rows.meaning: Use this to ask about the travel time.
rows.example: The bus is good. How long does it take?

rows.meaning: Use this to ask about the price before you pay.
rows.example: I want to take the train. How much is a ticket?

rows.term: Where can I buy a ticket?
rows.meaning: Use this when you do not know where to pay.
rows.example: I want the bus. Where can I buy a ticket?

blocks.title: Part 3: Your First Look at the Old Town
paragraphs: You arrive in the city. You walk into Vilnius Old Town. The Old Town is very old. Many of its streets and buildings are hundreds of years old. It is one of the largest old towns in Northern Europe. So you see many small streets and many old buildings.
You see two big squares. One is Cathedral Square. The other is Town Hall Square. You also see the buildings of Vilnius University. They are a famous part of the Old Town.

Then you see the Gate of Dawn. This is an important old gate. People built it between 1503 and 1514. It was part of the city wall. Later, people took down most of the city walls. But they kept this gate. It has a famous picture of the Virgin Mary. Many people come here to pray. The church services are in Lithuanian and Polish.

blocks.title: Check: Part 3: Your First Look at the Old Town

items.prompt: Why do many people still visit the Gate of Dawn today?
items.answer: It is an old gate from the city wall, and it has a famous picture of the Virgin Mary. Many people come to pray, and there are services in Lithuanian and Polish.

blocks.title: Part 4: You Check In and Ask for Help
paragraphs: You find your hotel. You go to the front desk. You say your name. You show your passport. The staff member gives you a key card. Now you have a room.

You are new in Vilnius, so ask for help. The front desk is a good place for questions. Ask for the Wi-Fi password. Ask for a map. Ask for the way to Cathedral Square or Town Hall Square. These are big squares in the Old Town, so they are easy places to meet people or start a walk.
You can ask about food too. Hotel staff know the area.

blocks.title: Check: Part 4: You Check In and Ask for Help

items.prompt: You are hungry, and your phone has no data. How can the hotel front desk help you?
items.answer: I can ask for the Wi-Fi password, a map and a good place for Lithuanian food near the hotel. The staff can show me the way on the map.

blocks.title: Useful phrases

rows.meaning: Use this when you arrive at the hotel desk.
rows.example: Hello, I have a reservation. My name is Sato.

rows.meaning: Use this to ask for help in a polite way.
rows.example: My phone has no data. Can you help me, please?

rows.term: Can you show me on the map?
rows.meaning: Use this when you want to see the way.
rows.example: Town Hall Square? Can you show me on the map?

blocks.title: Part 5: Your First Lithuanian Meal
paragraphs: You go to a restaurant near your hotel. You look at the menu.

You see two famous Lithuanian dishes. The first dish is cepelinai. They are big potato dumplings, often with meat inside. The cook boils them. They come with a sour cream sauce and small bits of bacon or pork rind. This is a warm, heavy meal. It is good after a long trip.

The second dish is šaltibarščiai. This is a cold soup, and it is bright pink. It has boiled and cooled beetroot, cucumber, green onion, dill and other herbs. The beetroot gives it the pink colour. People in Vilnius love this soup. Since 2023, Vilnius has a festival for this soup every year.
The menu shows the prices in euros. Read the price before you order.

blocks.title: Check: Part 5: Your First Lithuanian Meal

items.prompt: Why is šaltibarščiai pink, and why is it a good choice on a warm day?
items.answer: It is pink because of the beetroot. It is a cold soup with cucumber, green onion, dill and herbs, so it feels fresh on a warm day.

blocks.title: Useful phrases

rows.meaning: Use this to ask about the food in a dish.
rows.example: The pink soup looks nice. What is in it?

rows.term: I would like the cepelinai, please.
rows.meaning: Use this to order your food.
rows.example: I am very hungry. I would like the cepelinai, please.

rows.term: Can I have the bill, please?
rows.meaning: Use this at the end of a meal to pay.
rows.example: Thank you, it was great. Can I have the bill, please?

blocks.title: Scene: At the Airport Information Desk
paragraphs: You have your bag, and you are at the arrivals area of Vilnius Airport. Your hotel is in the Old Town. You see an information desk.
Your goal is to choose a ride to the Old Town and learn the time, the price and where to buy a ticket.

images.alt: At an airport information counter, the traveler and a staff member point to a city map, with her suitcase beside her and an airplane beyond the terminal windows.

blocks.title: Conversation: At the Airport Information Desk

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Hello. How can I get to the Old Town?

turns.speaker: Rūta
turns.text: Hello! You have three choices. You can take the train, the bus or a taxi.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: How long does it take?

turns.speaker: Rūta
turns.text: The train takes about 8 minutes to the railway station. The bus and the taxi take about 15 minutes.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: The train is fast! How much is a ticket?

turns.speaker: Rūta
turns.text: The train ticket costs €0.45. You can buy it online. But the train runs only 16 times a day. Please check the next train time.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Oh, I see. And the bus?

turns.speaker: Rūta
turns.text: The bus ticket costs €1. Several buses go to the city centre and the Old Town.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Where can I buy a ticket?

turns.speaker: Rūta
turns.text: You can buy it from the driver.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: And a taxi? I am a little tired.

turns.speaker: Rūta
turns.text: A taxi to Cathedral Square costs about €10. Taxis wait at arrivals. You can also use Bolt or Uber. They work all day and all night.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Thank you. I think I want the bus. It is cheap, and it goes to the Old Town.

turns.speaker: Rūta
turns.text: Good choice. Is this your first time in Lithuania?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Yes, it is. I am from Japan.

turns.speaker: Rūta
turns.text: Welcome to Vilnius! Enjoy the Old Town.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Thank you very much. Goodbye!

blocks.title: Scene: At the Hotel Front Desk
paragraphs: You walk through the Old Town and arrive at your hotel. You feel tired but happy.
Your goal is to check in, get help with your phone and ask about food and the way to Town Hall Square.

images.alt: At a wooden hotel reception desk, a traveler in a sage jacket holds a plain burgundy passport and receives a blank white key card, with her amber suitcase beside her.

blocks.title: Conversation: At the Hotel Front Desk

turns.speaker: Tomas
turns.text: Good evening. Welcome!

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Good evening. I have a reservation. My name is [your name].

turns.speaker: Tomas
turns.text: Yes, I see it. Can I have your passport, please?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Here you are.

turns.speaker: Tomas
turns.text: Thank you. Here is your key card.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Thank you. Can you help me, please? My phone has no data.

turns.speaker: Tomas
turns.text: Of course. Here is the Wi-Fi password. It is on this card.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Great, thank you. I also want to eat Lithuanian food tonight.

turns.speaker: Tomas
turns.text: There is a good restaurant on our street. Try the cepelinai. They come with sour cream sauce and bacon.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: That sounds good. Is there a cold soup too? A pink soup?

turns.speaker: Tomas
turns.text: Yes, šaltibarščiai! It is a cold beetroot soup. I eat it every summer.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I want to try it. And tomorrow I want to see Town Hall Square.

turns.speaker: Tomas
turns.text: It is a big square in the Old Town.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Can you show me on the map?

turns.speaker: Tomas
turns.text: Sure. We are here. Town Hall Square is here. The restaurant is here, near us.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Thank you, Tomas. You are very kind.

turns.speaker: Tomas
turns.text: You are welcome. Enjoy your dinner!

blocks.title: Scene: Dinner at a Lithuanian Restaurant
paragraphs: You find the restaurant near your hotel. It is warm and busy inside. A server named Eglė gives you a menu.
Your goal is to ask about the dishes, order your meal and pay.

images.alt: In a warm restaurant, a traveler in a sage jacket receives a plain menu from a server in a green apron, with other diners and Old Town buildings behind them.

blocks.title: Conversation: Dinner at a Lithuanian Restaurant

turns.speaker: Eglė
turns.text: Good evening! Here is the menu.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Thank you. This is my first day in Lithuania.

turns.speaker: Eglė
turns.text: Welcome! Do you want to try Lithuanian food?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Yes, please. The pink soup looks nice. What is in it?

turns.speaker: Eglė
turns.text: It has beetroot, cucumber, green onion, dill and some herbs. It is cold.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: A cold pink soup! We do not have this in Japan.

turns.speaker: Eglė
turns.text: People here love it. Vilnius has a festival for this soup every year.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Wow. I want the soup. I would like the cepelinai, please.

turns.speaker: Eglė
turns.text: Good choice. They come with sour cream sauce and bacon bits.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Perfect. I am very hungry after my trip.

turns.speaker: Eglė
turns.text: Here you are. Enjoy your meal!

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Thank you. It is really good.

turns.speaker: Eglė
turns.text: I am happy to hear that.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Can I have the bill, please?

turns.speaker: Eglė
turns.text: Of course. Here it is.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Here you are. Thank you for a great first dinner!

turns.speaker: Eglė
turns.text: Thank you. Have a nice time in Vilnius!

blocks.title: Speaking
paragraphs: Work with a partner. Tell the story of your first day in Vilnius. Use "I" and the present tense. Start at the airport and end at dinner. Choose the train, the bus or a taxi, and say the time and the price. Say one thing about the Old Town or the Gate of Dawn. Then order one dish. Your partner asks two questions, for example "Why do you choose the bus?" and "What is in the soup?" Then change roles.

blocks.title: Final Reflection
blocks.intro: You go from Vilnius Airport to your hotel in about 15 minutes, and the trip can cost €0.45, €1 or about €10. You see a very old town, check in with simple questions and try two famous Lithuanian dishes. Now you can plan this first day and talk about it in English.

items.prompt: Which ride from the airport do you choose, and why?
What do you want to see first in the Old Town?
Do you want to try cepelinai or šaltibarščiai first? Why?
